description: It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most. We need to rethink welfare for an economy being reshaped by AI. Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide. NOAA's Climate Prediction Center said on Nov. 12 that El Niño is still strengthening, with a greater-than-79 % chance of a strong-to-very-strong event between January and March 2027. That's down from 83% in its October update, but it’s still likely to produce adverse conditions, with wetter weather in the South and warmer weather in the North. description: Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan to flip yet another Senate seat for Democrats. Updated vote counts released Tuesday night gave Peltola just over 50% of the first-choice ballots, according to the Associated Press, allowing her to secure victory without having to rely on any second-choice ballots under the state's ranked-choice voting system. Peltola's victory comes after weeks of controversy, accusations and legal wrangling stemming from the presence of Daniel J. Sullivan — an unaffiliated candidate who happens to share a name with the incumbent Republican senator — on the ballot. Alaska's race was the last undecided Senate contest of the midterm cycle, which saw Democrats flip both chambers of Congress with substantial majorities. Peltola is the ninth Democrat to flip a GOP-held Senate seat this year. She is the first Democrat elected to the Senate in Alaska since 2008. description: South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.
